laura-p: Hey team — running into a weird one with /v1/rerank/batch. When we send multiple queries in one request, the returned scores sometimes appear shifted (scores don't match candidates) and occasionally the call returns a 502. Repro below.

laura-p: Request we sent (simplified):
```json
{
  "queries": ["how to reset password", "billing invoice missing"],
  "candidates": ["reset link steps", "contact support", "invoice pdf location", "billing team contact"]
}
```

laura-p: The intent was per-query candidates: [[reset link steps, contact support], [invoice pdf location, billing team contact]] — but we flattened into a single candidates array.

maria-support: Thanks — can you paste the trace_id from the failing request and confirm model + sdk version? Also Content-Type and any proxy in front? :eyes:

laura-p: trace=tr-9f3b2a, model=re-rank-1.3, sdk=redwood-python/0.9.2, Content-Type=application/json; no proxy (direct). We saw both 200 (but with misaligned scores) and 502s when payload size increases.

ryan-eng: Quick guess: the batch rerank endpoint expects per-query candidate lists (per_query_candidates or candidates_per_query), not a single flattened candidates array. Some older clients accidentally flatten and the server tried best-effort mapping which can cause index-shifts. If you can, try this payload:
```json
{
  "queries": ["how to reset password", "billing invoice missing"],
  "per_query_candidates": [
    ["reset link steps", "contact support"],
    ["invoice pdf location", "billing team contact"]
  ]
}
```

ryan-eng: Also note limits: max candidates per query = 512 and max combined token budget ~65536. If you exceed those, we may fallback or return 5xxs.

samir-oncall: Can you attach the raw request id and full headers from the 502 sample? If this is reproducible we should open an incident and quarantine the request in logs.

laura-p: Uploaded headers and raw body to the ticket (trace tr-9f3b2a). Quick workaround: we chunked each query into separate /v1/rerank calls (one query per request) and alignment fixed — but latency and cost went up.

ryan-eng: For production, prefer per_query_candidates or use our client-side chunking helper (redwood.sdk.rerank.chunk_requests) to keep larger batches from tripping server boundaries. We'll also add better validation so flattened lists return a 4xx with helpful message instead of silently shifting.

maria-support: Escalating to eng team with incident #INC-4839 — attaching traces and repro steps. We'll monitor canary for a config that rejects flattened candidate lists.

ingest-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled for rerank-validation v2 at 03:00 UTC.

laura-p: Thanks — please keep me posted. We're rolling the chunking workaround for now. :thumbsup:

ryan-eng: I'll follow up with a short snippet you can drop into our Python SDK to auto-detect flattened candidate arrays and rewrite them into per_query_candidates before sending. If you want I can paste it here.

laura-p: That'd be great, ty!

maria-support: Closing slack thread; tracking in ticket INC-4839. Will update when canary shows healthy and we have a client patch.
